algorithms.name: Pessimistic Risk-Aware Policy Learning (LCB maximization with IS/WIS/DR CDF estimators)

source.label: thm-ope
source.quote: Fix any policy $\pi \in \Pi$. For the clipped IS estimator $\Fisc^\pi$ ... it holds for any $\delta\in(0,1)$ that $\Pb ( \| \Fisc^\pi - F^\pi \|_\infty \leq ( \sigma_\pi + 1 ) \sqrt{\frac{8}{n}\log\frac{8}{\delta}} + r_\pi ) \geq 1-\delta.$

results.notes: Sup-norm CDF estimation error (off-policy evaluation), not regret. Theorem also gives a Bernstein-type variant with sigma'_pi and an extra 2log(8/delta)/(3n beta_min) term.

conditions: holds uniformly over all pi in Pi

source.label: thm-uniBound-IS
source.quote: define $R(\pi) \coloneq ( \sigma_\pi + 2 ) \sqrt{\frac{8}{n} [ \log\frac{20}{\delta} + d_{\Pi} \log(nK^2) ] } + r_\pi.$ Then, it holds $\Pb ( \| \Fisc^\pi - F^\pi \|_\infty \leq R(\pi), \forall \pi\in\Pi ) \geq 1-\delta.$

results.notes: Uniform CDF estimation error bound. WIS (Theorem 3) and DR (Theorem 4) analogues not recorded separately due to complex expressions.

bound.regime: log(20/delta) + d_Pi*log(n K^2) <= c_0 n beta_inf

symbols.beta_inf: overlap constant of optimal policy: inf_x beta(x,pi*) >= beta_inf
symbols.L_rho: Lipschitz constant of the risk functional w.r.t. sup norm on CDFs

conditions: log(20/delta) + d_Pi log(nK^2) <= c_0 n beta_inf
rho is L-Lipschitz w.r.t. sup norm over CDFs
quantity: risk suboptimality rho_{pi*} - rho_{tilde pi}

source.label: cor-bound-dr
source.quote: Suppose there exists a constant $\beta_{\inf}>0$ such that $\inf_{x\in\Xs}\beta(x,\pi^*)\geq \beta_{\inf}$, and that the sample size $n$ satisfies $\log(20/\delta) + d_{\Pi} \log(nK^2) \leq c_0 n\beta_{\inf}$. Then, for any constant $c \geq 8 (4\sqrt{2} + \frac{\sqrt{c_0}}{3})$ and any $\delta\in(0,1)$, it holds with probability at least $1-\delta$ that $\rho_{\pi^*} - \rho_{\tilde{\pi}} \leq c L \sqrt{ \frac{ d_{\Pi} \log(nK^2) \cdot \log(20/\delta) }{n\beta_{\inf}} }.$

results.notes: Suboptimality of learned policy under risk functional; quantity 'other' (risk-aware). Proof uses the Bernstein-type DR bound.

conditions: sup over environment/behavior-policy pairs with inf_x beta(x,pi*_v) >= beta_inf
any (possibly data-dependent) policy hat pi in Pi
quantity: expected 1-Wasserstein distance between CDFs of optimal and learned policies

source.label: thm-minimax
source.quote: Suppose the risk measure $\rho$ is monotone ... If $n\beta_{\inf}/d_{\Pi} \geq 2/3$, then for any (possibly data-dependent) policy $\hat{\pi}\in\Pi$, it holds that $\inf_{\hat{\pi}\in\Pi} \sup_{(v,\beta)\in\Vs} \Eb\,W_1( F^{\pi^*_v,v} , F^{\hat{\pi},v} ) \geq \frac{1}{8\sqrt{6e}}\sqrt{ \frac{d_\Pi}{n\beta_{\inf}} }$

results.notes: Bound is on expected W1 distance; under reverse-Lipschitz condition with L' it gives a risk-suboptimality lower bound times L'. Hard instances use Bernoulli rewards.
